title: stale cannot evaluate validity_conditions, so a lapsed condition is undetectable
description:
FINDING, made during T-399. This is the mechanical half of T-404.

precedent.py stale reports ONE check only: check=D [decay-candidate], citation decay, threshold
10 subsequent publications, 36 candidates across 59 records at the time of writing. It does not
read validity_conditions at all. Confirm that by reading the function before building anything.

CONSEQUENCE. Every tier-1 record in this layer states the conditions under which it stops being
valid, in prose, and NO TOOL IN THIS HARNESS CAN NOTICE WHEN ONE OF THEM STOPS HOLDING. T-404's
finding was made by a coordinator reading the record by hand while doing unrelated work. That is
not a detector.

WHAT TO BUILD, and the hard part is the honesty and not the code:
  A verb that lists each record's validity_conditions next to whatever the harness can actually
  measure about them, and that says plainly which ones it CANNOT evaluate.

The trap to refuse. A tool that pattern-matches prose and emits 'condition no longer holds' will
be wrong, and wrong in the expensive direction, because it would report a tier-1 record as
lapsed on a string match. Follow the currency.py precedent instead: emit the figure and refuse
the verdict. If a condition cannot be mechanically evaluated, the correct output names the
condition and prints NOT MECHANICALLY EVALUABLE. A report listing 59 records as 'unknown' is a
TRUE report and is more useful than a false one, because it tells a reader exactly how much of
this layer rests on nobody having checked.

Registry rules that apply. GUARD-MENTION-C: if any test scans source for a token, parse the AST
instead, because prose explaining a command will trip a substring scan. This is the fourth time
that defect would apply. TELEMETRY-PROVENANCE-A: report counts raw AND distinct, never one.

Ship with the count of conditions in each bucket, and pin the bucketing with tests.
acceptance_criteria: Read the stale implementation first and record verbatim which checks it runs; the claim 'validity_conditions are not evaluated' must be evidenced, not assumed.
A verb that lists every record's validity_conditions and, per condition, either a measured value or the literal NOT MECHANICALLY EVALUABLE.
NO pass/fail verdict on prose conditions. A false lapse report on a tier-1 record is the expensive failure; refuse the verdict as currency.py does.
Any test that inspects source parses the AST, never a substring scan (GUARD-MENTION-C, fourth occurrence).
T-404's finding appears in the output when the verb runs against the live registry: PR-022's condition is listed, and listed as one this tool cannot evaluate.
Full suite green; negative control run and reported for at least one test per group.
